chunks: And from him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya ibn 'Imran, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"If you wish, pray the Salat al-Tasbih at night; and if you wish, [pray it] during the day; and if you wish, [pray it] while traveling; and if you wish, make it part of your voluntary prayers; and if you wish, make it from the makeup of a missed prayer."
And in the narration of Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him):
"It is recited in the first [rak'ah] 'When the earth is shaken', in the second 'By the runners [horses]', in the third 'When the help of Allah comes', and in the fourth 'Say: He is Allah, One'"

I said, 'What is its reward?' He said, 'If there were upon him as many sins as the sand of 'Araj, Allah would forgive him.' Then he looked at me and said, 'That is specifically for you and your companions.'

key_terms.رَمْلُ عَالِجٍ: The sand of 'Araj (a metaphor for a vast quantity)

ai.seo_question: How is the voluntary prayer of Salat al-Tasbih performed and what are its specific rewards?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the versatility of Salat al-Tasbih, a highly recommended voluntary prayer, by permitting its performance at any time or place and allowing it to serve either as *nafl* (supererogatory) or *qada* (makeup) for obligatory prayers. The narration specifies the recitation of Surahs Al-Zalzalah, Al-Adiyat, Al-Nasr, and Al-Ikhlas in the four rak'ahs, linking the ritual to the themes of resurrection, divine victory, and monotheism. The Imam highlights the immense reward of sin forgiveness, extending this specific merit to the narrator and his companions, underscoring the prayer's spiritual efficacy in Shia tradition.
